ei.title: Why Scientific Experiments Require Manipulation and Control
ei.subject: 6월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Why Scientific Experiments Require Manipulation and Control

fullPassage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if ①<u>there're</u> a difference. At the same time, they ②<u>attempt</u> to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely ③<u>observe</u> the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to ④<u>create</u> a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① there're → there's: 뒤의 명사가 단수 a difference이므로 there is(there's)가 맞음
det.analysis:
✅ ① there're — 원문은 there's(there is)예요. 'see if __________ a difference(차이가 있는지 본다)'에서 뒤의 명사가 단수 a difference라, there is의 축약형 there's가 맞아요. there're(there are)는 복수용이라 틀려요. ←정답

❌ ② attempt — 'they attempt to control(통제하려 시도한다)'. 복수주어 they에 맞아요.

❌ ③ observe — 'we can't merely observe(단지 관찰만 할 순 없다)'. 조동사 뒤 동사원형이라 맞아요.

❌ ④ create — 'we have to create a situation(상황을 만들어야 한다)'. have to 뒤 동사원형이라 맞아요.
det.tip: 뒤 명사가 단수 a difference → there's(there is)

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists ①<u>manipulate</u> a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people ②<u>who takes</u> vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want ③<u>to study</u> the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while ④<u>holding</u> everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② who takes → who take: 선행사 people이 복수이므로 관계절 동사도 복수 take가 맞음
det.analysis:
❌ ① manipulate — 'Scientists manipulate a variable(변수를 조작한다)'. 복수주어에 맞아요.

✅ ② who takes — 원문은 who take예요. 관계대명사 who의 선행사가 복수 people이라, 관계절 동사도 복수 take가 맞아요. takes는 틀려요. ←정답

❌ ③ to study — 'if we want to study(연구하고 싶다면)'. want 뒤 to부정사라 맞아요.

❌ ④ holding — 'while holding everything else constant'. while 뒤 분사라 맞아요.
det.tip: 선행사 people(복수) → who take

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they ①<u>attempt</u> to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who ②<u>take</u> vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation ③<u>what doesn't</u> actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while ④<u>holding</u> everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ what doesn't → that doesn't: 선행사 a situation을 꾸미는 관계절이므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which)이 맞음
det.analysis:
❌ ① attempt — 'they attempt to control'. 복수주어 they에 맞아요.

❌ ② take — 'people who take vitamin supplements'. 복수 선행사 people에 맞아요.

✅ ③ what doesn't — 원문은 that doesn't예요. 앞에 선행사 'a situation'이 있고 이를 꾸미는 관계절이므로 관계대명사 that(또는 which)을 써야 해요. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 선행사가 있는 자리엔 쓸 수 없어 틀려요. ←정답

❌ ④ holding — 'while holding everything else constant'. while 뒤 분사라 맞아요.
det.tip: 선행사(a situation) 있음 → 관계대명사 that/which (what ✗)

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often ①<u>separate</u>. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely ②<u>observe</u> the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to ③<u>create</u> a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else ④<u>constant</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① separate → correlated: 통제되지 않은 현실에서 변수들은 흔히 '상관된다(correlated)'가 맞으므로 '분리된(separate)'은 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① separate(분리된) — 원문은 correlated예요. 뒤에 '비타민 먹는 사람은 식사·운동 습관도 다르다'는 예가 나오듯, 현실에서는 변수들이 '서로 상관된다'는 것이 핵심이라 '분리된'은 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

❌ ② observe(관찰하다): '현실을 관찰만 할 순 없다' — 맞아요.

❌ ③ create(만들다): '현실에 없는 상황을 만들어야 한다' — 맞아요.

❌ ④ constant(일정한): '나머지를 일정하게 유지' — 맞아요.
det.tip: 현실 = 변수들이 '상관됨(correlated)', separate는 반대

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists ①<u>manipulate</u> a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The ②<u>triviality</u> of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely ③<u>observe</u> the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to ④<u>separate</u> the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② triviality → importance: 통제된 실험의 '중요성(importance)'은 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않다가 맞으므로 '사소함(triviality)'은 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① manipulate(조작하다): '변수를 조작한다' — 맞아요.

✅ ② triviality(사소함) — 원문은 importance예요. 'The __________ of controlled experiments ... cannot be overstated(통제된 실험의 ___은 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않다)'에서, 글이 통제된 실험을 매우 중시하므로 '중요성'이 맞고 '사소함'은 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

❌ ③ observe(관찰하다): '현실을 관찰만 할 순 없다' — 맞아요.

❌ ④ separate(분리하다): '자연히 얽힌 관계를 분리하려 한다' — 맞아요.
det.tip: cannot be overstated(강조해도 지나치지 않다) → importance(중요성)

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to __________ of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: control for the potential effects — 다른 모든 변수의 '잠재적 영향을 통제'하려 함
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'they attempt to __________ of all other variables'예요. 앞에서 실험법의 본질이 조작과 '통제'라고 했으니, 다른 변수들의 영향을 통제한다는 내용이어야 해요.

✅ ③ control for the potential effects(잠재적 영향을 통제하다): 실험의 핵심인 '통제'와 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ① measure the exact size(정확한 크기를 측정하다): 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ② ignore the hidden causes(숨은 원인을 무시하다): 통제와 반대예요.

❌ ④ increase the random noise(무작위 잡음을 늘리다): 실험 취지와 반대예요.
det.tip: 실험법 = 다른 변수의 '잠재적 영향을 통제(control for)'

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have __________ than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: different eating and exercise habits — 비타민 먹는 사람은 '다른 식사·운동 습관'을 가질 수 있어 변수가 얽힘
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 변수들이 상관된다는 예시로, 'people who take vitamin supplements may have __________ than people who don't take vitamins(비타민 먹는 사람은 안 먹는 사람과 ___이 다를 수 있다)'예요. 변수가 서로 얽힌다는 핵심을 보여줘야 해요.

✅ ① different eating and exercise habits(다른 식사·운동 습관): 비타민 복용이 식사·운동 같은 다른 요인과 함께 묶여 인과를 흐린다는 흐름에 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② the same genetic background(같은 유전적 배경): 변수가 '다름'을 보여주지 못해요.

❌ ③ no interest in their health(건강에 무관심): 비약이에요.

❌ ④ a much shorter life expectancy(훨씬 짧은 기대수명): 본문에 없는 단정이에요.
det.tip: 비타민 복용자 ↔ 다른 '식사·운동 습관'이 함께 얽힘

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 현실 변수들은 '상관되어' 있어 관찰만으론 인과를 알 수 없으므로 불일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① 'The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control'과 일치해요.

❌ ② 'they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables'와 일치해요.

❌ ③ 'people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits'와 일치해요.

✅ ④ 본문은 현실에서 변수들이 '상관되어(correlated)' 있어 단지 관찰만으론 인과를 알 수 없다고 했어요. '독립적이어서 쉽게 알 수 있다'는 정반대라 일치하지 않아요. ←정답
det.tip: 현실 변수 = 상관됨 → 관찰만으론 인과 못 밝힘

ch: 과학자들은 다른 모든 변수의 잠재적 영향을 통제하려 한다.
비타민을 먹는 사람은 식사·운동 습관이 다를 수 있다.
현실 세계에서는 변수들이 서로 독립적이어서 인과를 쉽게 알 수 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 과학 실험은 현실에 없는 상황을 '만들어낸다'고 했으므로 '그대로 관찰한다'는 불일치
det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문은 과학 실험이 'a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world(현실에서 실제로는 일어나지 않는 상황)'를 만들어낸다고 했어요. '자연스러운 상황을 그대로 관찰한다'는 정반대라 일치하지 않아요. ←정답

❌ ② 'The importance of controlled experiments ... cannot be overstated'와 일치해요.

❌ ③ 'Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference'와 일치해요.

❌ ④ 'manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant'와 일치해요.
det.tip: 실험은 현실에 없는 상황을 '만듦' (관찰만 ✗)

ch: 과학 실험은 현실에서 흔히 일어나는 자연스러운 상황을 그대로 관찰한다.
통제된 실험의 중요성은 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않다.
과학자들은 관심 변수를 조작해 차이가 있는지 살핀다.
실험은 한 변수만 조작하고 나머지를 일정하게 유지한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ② 여러 요인이 얽혀 있어 '관찰만으로는' 효과를 알 수 없다고 했으므로 불일치
det.analysis:
❌ ① 'any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health'와 일치해요.

✅ ② 본문은 비타민·식단·운동이 모두 건강에 영향을 줄 수 있어 '단지 현실을 관찰만 해서는(merely observe)' 효과를 알 수 없다고 했어요. '관찰만 해도 분명히 드러난다'는 정반대라 일치하지 않아요. ←정답

❌ ④ 'They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world'와 일치해요.
det.tip: 관찰만으론 효과 못 밝힘 (② 반대)

ch: 비타민, 식단, 운동은 모두 건강에 영향을 줄 수 있다.
비타민의 건강 효과는 현실을 관찰하기만 해도 분명히 드러난다.
과학 실험은 현실에 없는 상황을 만들어낸다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
